newsitem.title: USA: Baxter wins verdict in Dallas implant case.
newsitem.headline: Baxter wins verdict in Dallas implant case.

text.p: Baxter Healthcare Corp, a unit of Baxter International Inc, in a release received here, said a Dallas County (Texas) jury has returned verdicts in favor of the company after three weeks of trial in a breast implant case involving two plaintiffs.
It said the jury deliberated about two hours before deciding 10 to 2 in finding no negligence, product defect, fraud or violation of the Texas Consumer Protection Act.
Baxter now has won 23 verdicts in breast implant lawsuits. Two cases ended in mistrials, and three cases originally lost are either on appeal or being re-tried.

The company has never manufactured nor marketed breast implants. Its contractual liability is a result of a 1985 merger with American Hospital Supply Corp, which at one time had owned breast implant manufacturer Heyer-Schulte Corp. American divested Heyer-Schulte in 1984, and the company no longer exists.
Deerfield, Ill.-based Baxter was represented in the Dallas case by Russell Schell of Schell, Beene & Vaughan.
